questions.def: Future perfect indicates completion before a future time.
questions.question: By next year, she ___ her PhD.

questions.def: Scheduled events use 'is scheduled to' for formal future.
questions.question: The train ___ at 6:00 AM tomorrow.

questions.def: Future trends with evidence use continuous forms.
questions.question: Experts ___ that the economy will improve.

questions.def: 'Shall' expresses formal future intent or presumption.
questions.question: I ___ be seeing you at the conference, I presume?

questions.def: 'Is bound to' shows strong likelihood based on evidence.
questions.question: He ___ be promoted, given his performance.

questions.def: 'Intends' shows a present intention for the future.
questions.question: She ___ to submit the proposal by Friday.

questions.def: 'Are to' indicates a planned or official future event.
questions.question: The results ___ be announced next week.

questions.def: 'Should' creates a formal conditional sentence.
questions.question: ___ you require further assistance, please contact us.

questions.def: 'Anticipate' expresses a future expectation.
questions.question: We ___ a large turnout at the event.

questions.def: 'Should have' expresses an expected past action.
questions.question: They ___ have arrived by now; the flight was on time.

questions.def: 'Was to' expresses a planned but unfulfilled action.
questions.question: He ___ have finished the report, but he was delayed.

questions.def: 'Expect' indicates a present belief about the future.
questions.question: I ___ that the project will be successful.

questions.def: 'Unless' introduces a conditional statement.
questions.question: ___ I be mistaken, he will arrive tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Come what may' expresses determination regardless of outcome.
questions.question: Come what ___, I will finish this task.

questions.def: 'Aim' expresses a current intention.
questions.question: We ___ to complete the project by June.

questions.def: 'In the event of' introduces a conditional clause.
questions.question: ___ the event of rain, the ceremony will be moved indoors.

questions.def: 'Is expected to' indicates a passive future expectation.
questions.question: She ___ to have finished the book by next week.

questions.def: 'Hope' expresses a current wish for the future.
questions.question: I ___ to see you again soon.

questions.def: 'It would appear' indicates a tentative prediction.
questions.question: It ___ appear that the negotiations will succeed.

questions.def: 'Is highly likely' expresses a strong probability.
questions.question: He ___ likely to accept the offer.

questions.def: Future perfect with time clauses uses present simple.
questions.question: She will have finished the report by the time he arrives.

questions.def: 'Assume' expresses a present belief about the future.
questions.question: We ___ that he will be on time.

questions.def: 'Despite' introduces a contrasting fact.
questions.question: ___ being delayed, they managed to arrive on time.

questions.def: 'Is to arrive' indicates a formal or scheduled future arrival.
questions.question: She ___ shortly.

questions.def: Future perfect 'will have completed' shows an action completed before a future time.
questions.question: By the time the report is due, I ___ all the research.

questions.def: 'Is due to meet' expresses a formal, scheduled future event.
questions.question: The committee ___ next Tuesday to discuss the proposal.

questions.def: Present continuous 'is embarking' expresses a planned future event.
questions.question: The ship ___ on its maiden voyage next month.

questions.def: 'Should rain' expresses a less probable future condition.
questions.question: If it ___, the outdoor event will be cancelled.

questions.def: 'Will prove' expresses a strong expectation about a future outcome.
questions.question: I fully expect that the negotiations ___ successful.

questions.def: 'Are to complete' expresses a formal obligation or arrangement.
questions.question: We ___ the project by the end of the week.
